article_title: PEP 836 Authors Withdraw Their CPython JIT Proposal, and Brett Cannon Says the Withdrawal Means the JIT Will Come Out of main

content_preview.title: PEP 836 Authors Withdraw Their CPython JIT Proposal, and Brett Cannon Says the Withdrawal Means the JIT Will Come Out of main
content_preview.summary: The authors of PEP 836 withdrew it on October 19; Brett Cannon wrote that the JIT work stops in CPython's repo, after the Steering Council's June six-month condition for keeping it in main.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

PEP 836, the proposal that was meant to justify keeping CPython's experimental JIT compiler in the main branch, has been withdrawn by its authors. Savannah Ostrowski wrote on October 19 in the [PEP's discussion thread](https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-836-jit-go-brrr-the-path-to-a-supported-jit-compiler-for-cpython/108010): "After further discussion, we have decided to withdraw PEP 836." editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, What We Know, What We Don't Know), 767 words (News range 400-1200). Reports a withdrawal and the statements of named participants without inferring beyond them; Cannon's view is explicitly labelled as that of one participant.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three gzipped snapshots (source-0, source-1, source-2; all status 200, suspicious_patterns null for each) and re-fetched live. The snapshots of the two Discourse threads contain only the first ~20 posts (paginated), so posts 21-66 of the PEP 836 thread were re-fetched live through the Discourse JSON endpoint and each post's username/name/created_at field was checked (the thread had 66 posts at the time of review; last post #66 on 2026-10-21T08:27Z). The peps.python.org live page is byte-for-byte text-identical to the snapshot. source-0 (Steering Council announcement, discuss.python.org/t/107638): post #1 by username pablogsal (Pablo Galindo Salgado), June 5, 2026 12:56pm, signed 'The Python Steering Council'. Contains verbatim: 'We are setting a window of six months for a PEP to be submitted and resolved. If no such PEP is accepted within that window, the JIT code must be removed from the main branch and development must be continued outside the main Python repository.' Post #5 by pablogsal confirms 'This is a first goal to anchor, not a bureaucratic deadline we will hold' (article quote verbatim). source-1 (PEP 836 thread, discuss.python.org/t/108010): post #57 by savannahostrowski (Savannah Ostrowski), 2026-10-19T20:35Z: 'After further discussion, we have decided to withdraw PEP 836. The Steering Council rightly sets a high bar for a proposal of this scope, and we don't feel we have the personal bandwidth to carry the current version forward. We continue to believe in the technical direction outlined in the PEP, including free-threaded support and a method-based frontend, ... We'll make the reference implementation available and link it from the withdrawn PEP so others who are interested can explore and build on that.' All four article quotes verbatim. Post #49 by barry (Barry Warsaw), 2026-09-08T00:17Z (evening of Sept 7 in US time zones): 'the Steering Council has not been formally asked to pronounce on PEP 836' verbatim. Post #53 by thomas (Thomas Wouters), 2026-09-21: '(Posting for the Steering Council, minus Savannah as PEP co-author)', 'We're not evaluating, at this point, whether the JIT should be declared a supported feature', memory impact and security among the listed points, compatibility review 'way, way too late' in 'the last half year' of the timeline, and the 'Bottom line' sentence incl. ellipsis, all verbatim. Post #55 by kj0 (Ken Jin), 2026-09-25: 'We will work on it!' (article quotes 'work on it'). Brett Cannon: post #59 by barry-scott (Barry Scott) asks 'Does this mean that the JIT work is stopped?'; post #61 by brettcannon (Brett Cannon), 2026-10-20T16:33Z, replying to Barry Scott: 'In CPython's repo, yes. Whether others in the community organize to keep it going is up to the community.' and, replying to Sacul (post #60, who worried about 'the 6 months window for the JIT to be kept in Main'): 'The point of the PEP was to justify the JIT work staying in main, so the withdrawal of the PEP means it will come out and live somewhere else' (followed in the original by a parenthetical re-quoting Savannah's reference-implementation sentence, which the article omits without distortion). Post #62 by duncathan (Dunc Graham) asks whether an alternative PEP could still be submitted; post #63 by brettcannon: 'Not really as all the people actively driving the JIT were either authors on that PEP or contributors to it. Plus this decision was made at the core dev sprints where most of the people working on the JIT currently are, ...' (article quotes verbatim). Post #64 by h-vetinari (H. Vetinari), 2026-10-21T02:43Z: 'Would be nice to have an insight into what were the deciding factors for the decision to abandon this effort (at least in its current form).' (article quote verbatim; post #66 by timkofu merely seconds it). source-2 (peps.python.org/pep-0836): Authors listed as Savannah Ostrowski, Ken Jin, Brandt Bucher; Status Withdrawn; Resolution 19-Oct-2026; abstract has 'part of CPython's main branch since Python 3.13', 'about 4-12% geometric mean performance improvement across measured Tier 1 platforms', the 20% geometric mean target by the first beta of Python 3.17 and 'a minimum bar for continued in-tree development of the JIT' - all verbatim/accurate. Ostrowski is thus identified as a PEP author by the PEP page and as the withdrawing poster by post #57. LWN is not cited and nothing relies on it. No source is cited in the body that is missing from article.sources (orphan-link diff empty both ways).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every quote, number, date and attribution traced to the post author field. Title attribution: 'Brett Cannon Says the Withdrawal Means the JIT Will Come Out of main' matches post #61 (he writes that the withdrawal 'means it will come out and live somewhere else', answering a question about the 6-month window for the JIT to stay in main). The article presents it as 'per one participant' and states no role for Cannon; he does not claim to speak for the Steering Council and the article does not suggest he does. No Steering Council reply to the withdrawal exists in the live thread (re-checked 2026-10-27: 66 posts, last post 2026-10-21T08:27Z, none from a Council member after Ostrowski's post), and H. Vetinari's question about the deciding factors is unanswered. Internal link /article/2026-07/11-cpython-community-answers-steering-councils-six-month-jit-ultimatum-with-pep-836-a-path-to-a-supported-compiler resolves to a published article and is described accurately as the earlier report of the Council's six-month condition; nothing contradicts it. Minor notes: Warsaw's post is dated Sept 8 UTC (Sept 7 evening US time) and the article uses UTC dates consistently; Cannon's post has a trailing parenthetical (omitted) and the article's quote lacks closing punctuation, which is cosmetic.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual; no editorializing about the authors, the Council or the withdrawal. Statements by named people are reported as theirs. 'Per one participant' framing correctly limits the weight of Cannon's interpretation. No defamatory implications.
editor_notes.originality: Follow-up to the July 11 article on PEP 836 (a new development: withdrawal on October 19). Not a duplicate; no other article covers the withdrawal.
concerns: Cannon's reading that the JIT will leave main is one participant's interpretation; the Steering Council has not publicly confirmed or addressed it (flexibility on the deadline was previously stated by Galindo Salgado and Wouters). The article handles this correctly in What We Don't Know. A follow-up is warranted if the Council posts a formal statement on the JIT's removal or the reasons for withdrawal.
recommendations: Consider a follow-up when the Steering Council or the PEP authors publish a statement, the reference implementation link appears on the withdrawn PEP, or the JIT removal from main is scheduled.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed News article; all quotes verbatim and attributed to the correct post authors; no corrections needed. Featured candidacy: 2 - the possible removal of CPython's JIT from main is significant for the broad Python developer audience, though not yet confirmed by the Steering Council.
